questions.statement: A sovereign wealth fund has a strict regulatory requirement mandating that cryptographic encryption keys must be generated, stored, and managed inside dedicated, single-tenant FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) directly under the sole physical and logical control of the company's security officers. AWS personnel must have zero administrative access to the HSM key material. Which AWS service meets these compliance requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to provision and automatically renew public SSL/TLS certificates.
options.explanation: Incorrect: ACM manages SSL/TLS public certificates, not custom corporate symmetric HSM encryption keys.

options.text: Deploy an AWS CloudHSM cluster inside a private VPC to manage single-tenant FIPS 140-2 Level 3 cryptographic hardware.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated, single-tenant FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security modules running in your VPC where the customer has sole ownership and control of cryptographic keys and HSM user administration.

options.text: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) with multi-tenant default key stores
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard AWS KMS uses multi-tenant HSMs validated to FIPS 140-2 Level 3 (or Level 2) managed by AWS, rather than dedicated customer-administered single-tenant appliances.

options.text: Store application configuration feature flags in AWS Secrets Manager and schedule automatic secret rotation.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Secrets Manager stores database credentials and API keys, relying on KMS or CloudHSM for key encryption.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS CloudHSM provides fully managed, dedicated single-tenant hardware security modules (HSMs) under customer control for strict regulatory and FIPS 140-2 Level 3 compliance.

questions.statement: A global managed service provider (MSP) manages 500 AWS accounts under a consolidated billing AWS Organization. The MSP needs to generate customized pro forma billing invoices for different enterprise clients, apply custom markup rates and tiered pricing discounts, and allow clients to view their customized billing rates in their own consoles without exposing the MSP's actual wholesale AWS volume discounts. Which AWS service is designed for this requirement?

options.text: Use AWS Cost Explorer to visualize consolidated historical AWS expenditure and forecast future usage.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Cost Explorer displays actual historical AWS costs and discounts across consolidated billing, without custom client markup engines.

options.text: Use AWS Pricing Calculator to model architecture costs before provisioning AWS infrastructure resources.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Pricing Calculator is an architecture estimation tool, not an automated live multi-account billing customization engine.

options.text: Configure AWS Billing Conductor to define custom billing groups, apply pricing markups, and generate pro forma invoices.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Billing Conductor is a customizable billing service that allows MSPs and enterprises to customize billing rates, group accounts into billing groups, and generate pro forma billing views for end clients.

options.text: Configure AWS Budgets to send automated notifications when monthly spending limits exceed predefined thresholds.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Budgets sends spending alerts, but does not calculate custom rate markups or generate pro forma billing invoices.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Billing Conductor enables customers and MSPs to customize billing parameters, create billing groups, apply custom pricing rules, and present pro forma invoices to end users.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: An enterprise needs to implement centralized outbound internet egress inspection for 80 VPCs across 2 AWS Regions. All outbound web requests must be inspected against TLS Server Name Indication (SNI) domain whitelists and intrusion prevention system (IPS) Suricata rule sets. The solution must scale to 45 Gbps of egress traffic per region with high availability across 3 Availability Zones and zero single point of failure. Which architecture should be deployed?

options.text: Deploy a centralized Egress Inspection VPC in each region containing an AWS Transit Gateway attachment with Appliance Mode enabled, and deploy AWS Network Firewall endpoints in a dedicated firewall subnet in each Availability Zone backed by a stateful rule group for domain list SNI filtering and IPS Suricata rules.
options.explanation: Correct: Centralized egress inspection via AWS Transit Gateway with Appliance Mode and AWS Network Firewall endpoints across 3 AZs scales up to 100 Gbps, provides stateful SNI domain filtering, and eliminates single points of failure.

options.text: Deploy squid proxy EC2 instances on a single t3.medium instance in each spoke VPC.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed proxy instances on t3.medium cannot handle 45 Gbps, create single points of failure, and introduce massive operational maintenance.

options.text: Configure Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones in each VPC with wildcard records pointing to 127.0.0.1.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Route 53 DNS sinkholing does not provide stateful Layer 7 IPS packet inspection or SNI filtering for active TCP flows.

options.text: Create VPC Peering connections between all 80 VPCs and deploy NAT Gateways in every spoke subnet.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Deploying NAT Gateways in hundreds of spoke subnets is extremely expensive and lacks centralized stateful IPS/SNI inspection.

questions.generalExplanation: Centralized egress VPC architecture with AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Network Firewall provides scalable, highly available Layer 7 domain filtering and Suricata-compatible IPS inspection.

questions.statement: An automated data processing pipeline running on an EC2 instance in Account A needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket in Account B. For enhanced security, Account B requires that the IAM role in Account A must provide an External ID when assuming the cross-account role to prevent the 'Confused Deputy' problem. How should the IAM trust policy in Account B be configured?

options.text: Create an IAM user in Account B with an access key and send the plaintext secret key to Account A via email.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Distributing static long-term IAM credentials violates security best practices and does not solve the confused deputy vulnerability.

options.text: Add a public read/write bucket policy on the S3 bucket in Account B.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Making the bucket public exposes all data to the internet.

options.text: Configure the trust policy of the IAM role in Account B with an `sts:AssumeRole` action, specifying Account A's role as the Principal, and add a `Condition` block requiring `sts:ExternalId` matching the shared unique identifier string.
options.explanation: Correct: The Confused Deputy problem is mitigated by requiring the third-party/cross-account role assumption to supply an `sts:ExternalId` in the `Condition` block of the IAM role's trust policy.

options.text: Configure VPC Peering and disable IAM authorization entirely.
options.explanation: Incorrect: VPC Peering operates at the network layer and does not bypass or configure IAM role trust authorization.

questions.generalExplanation: Using an External ID in the `Condition` block of an IAM role's trust policy is the standard AWS mechanism to prevent the Confused Deputy problem during cross-account role assumption.

questions.statement: An enterprise runs 1,000 Amazon EC2 Windows Server instances across multiple AWS accounts in an AWS Organization. The instances must be joined seamlessly to an Active Directory domain for centralized Group Policy Objects (GPOs) and Kerberos authentication. The company wants to minimize on-premises domain controller traffic over Direct Connect and eliminate manual domain-join scripting. Which solution is most appropriate?

options.text: Point all 1,000 EC2 instances across all accounts directly to on-premises domain controller IP addresses over the public internet.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Exposing Active Directory ports over the public internet is a major security vulnerability and creates high network latency.

options.text: Create local Windows Administrator users on every EC2 instance using EC2 User Data.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Local user management on 1,000 instances lacks centralized domain governance, GPOs, and Kerberos SSO.

options.text: Deploy Amazon Cognito User Pools and configure Windows login via OAuth 2.0.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Windows Server Active Directory domain join and GPOs require native Microsoft Active Directory / Kerberos / LDAP, not Cognito.

options.text: Deploy AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) in a shared Services account, establish a two-way forest trust to the on-premises Active Directory, share the directory with member accounts via AWS RAM, and use AWS Systems Manager Seamless Domain Join.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Managed Microsoft AD deployed in AWS with a forest trust to on-prem AD allows low-latency local domain authentication in AWS, and SSM Seamless Domain Join automates domain joining across accounts without custom scripts.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Managed Microsoft AD shared across accounts combined with a forest trust and AWS Systems Manager Seamless Domain Join provides a scalable, highly available enterprise directory architecture.

Which solution enables this automated workflow?

options.text: Use AWS Control Tower Account Factory integrated with the AWS Service Catalog ServiceNow connector (or Account Factory for Terraform - AFT) to automate end-to-end account provisioning upon ticket approval.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Control Tower Account Factory and Account Factory for Terraform (AFT) automate standard account creation, governance guardrails, and network provisioning via API/ITSM integration.

options.text: Instruct an administrator to manually log in to the AWS Management Console to create accounts one by one.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Manual console account creation is slow, error-prone, and cannot integrate automatically with ServiceNow ticket approvals.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Lambda function that calls `create-user` across all accounts.
options.explanation: Incorrect: `create-user` creates individual IAM users, not complete new AWS accounts within AWS Organizations.

options.text: Attach a Service Control Policy (SCP) to ServiceNow's IP address.
options.explanation: Incorrect: SCPs are applied to AWS Organizations OUs and accounts, not external third-party IP addresses.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Control Tower Account Factory and Account Factory for Terraform (AFT) automate standardized, governed multi-account provisioning integrated with enterprise ITSM tools like ServiceNow.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A multinational financial enterprise stores 10 petabytes of historical transaction files in an Amazon S3 bucket in us-east-1. To meet new disaster recovery and data residency compliance requirements, all newly uploaded objects AND all existing 10 petabytes of historical objects must be replicated to a secondary bucket in eu-west-1. The objects are encrypted with an AWS KMS customer managed key (SSE-KMS). What combination of actions must be taken to replicate both new and existing data?

options.text: Enable S3 Versioning on both buckets, configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) with KMS encryption options and a destination KMS key specified, and initiate an Amazon S3 Batch Replication job to replicate the pre-existing objects.
options.explanation: Correct: Standard S3 CRR replicates only newly uploaded objects after the rule is created. Replicating existing objects requires creating an Amazon S3 Batch Replication job in addition to configuring CRR with SSE-KMS permissions.

options.text: Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) and wait 24 hours for AWS to automatically synchronize all historical objects.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard S3 CRR rules do NOT automatically replicate objects that existed prior to rule creation without an S3 Batch Replication job.

options.text: Use the AWS CLI command `aws s3 cp` on an EC2 t3.nano instance over the public internet.
options.explanation: Incorrect: An EC2 t3.nano instance will run out of memory, take months to transfer 10 PB over the internet, and cost substantially more than native S3 Batch Replication.

options.text: Change the storage class of the source bucket to S3 Glacier Flexible Archive to trigger automatic cross-region mirroring.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storage class transitions do not replicate data across AWS regions.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 Batch Replication allows you to replicate existing objects that were stored in a bucket prior to configuring S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR).

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A global gaming company is developing an active-active multiplayer game platform deployed across three AWS Regions: us-east-1, eu-central-1, and ap-northeast-1. Players must be able to read and write player inventory data locally in their closest region with single-digit millisecond latency, and data must be replicated bidirectionally across all three regions with automatic conflict resolution based on timestamps. Which database solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Amazon RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ with cross-region read replicas in all three regions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: RDS read replicas are read-only; they do not allow active-active local transactional writes in secondary regions.

options.text: Amazon DocumentDB with periodic S3 export and import jobs.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Periodic S3 export/import introduces hours of latency and does not support real-time active-active multi-region replication.

options.text: Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables (version 2019.11.21) deployed across all three regions with auto-scaling configured.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables provides fully managed, active-active multi-region replication with local read/write latency in single-digit milliseconds and automatic 'last-writer-wins' conflict resolution.

options.text: Configure and deploy Amazon Redshift cross-region snapshot copy. following AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Redshift is an analytical data warehouse, not a real-time transactional gaming database.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables enables fully managed active-active multi-region data replication, delivering local sub-10ms read/write latency across global user bases.

questions.statement: A corporate enterprise runs business-critical Windows applications on Amazon EC2 instances and on-premises Windows servers. The applications require a fully managed, shared Microsoft Windows file system that supports SMB protocol, Windows NTFS file permissions, Microsoft Active Directory integration, DFS Namespaces, and Multi-AZ high availability with sub-millisecond latency. Which storage service should the architect choose?

options.text: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Max I/O mode.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon EFS is an NFSv4 file system designed for Linux environments, and does not support Windows SMB or native NTFS ACLs.

options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server deployed in a Multi-AZ configuration integrated with Microsoft Active Directory.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is built on Windows Server, providing native SMB support, NTFS permissions, Active Directory integration, DFS Namespaces, and Multi-AZ automatic failover.

questions.statement: An e-commerce marketplace with millions of product listings needs to implement an intelligent search autocomplete and full-text search capability supporting fuzzy matching, typo tolerance, synonyms, and faceted filtering (by brand, price, rating). options.text: Stream DynamoDB item modifications via DynamoDB Streams to an AWS Lambda function that indexes documents into Amazon OpenSearch Service, and direct search queries from client applications to OpenSearch Service.
options.explanation: Correct: DynamoDB Streams + Lambda provides near real-time synchronization of database records into Amazon OpenSearch Service, which is purpose-built for fuzzy matching, faceting, and typo-tolerant full-text search.

options.text: Store all product descriptions in Amazon S3 and run Amazon Athena SQL queries on every user keystroke.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Athena queries take seconds to execute and are not suitable for sub-100ms real-time search autocomplete bars.

options.text: Execute DynamoDB `Scan` operations with complex filter expressions on every keystroke typed by users in the search bar.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Running `Scan` queries across millions of items on every keystroke consumes massive RCUs, introduces severe latency, and does not support fuzzy typo matching.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to execute SQL full-text queries.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Memcached is a simple in-memory key-value cache, not a search engine with full-text tokenizers and synonym filters.

questions.generalExplanation: Combining Amazon DynamoDB as the transactional data store with Amazon OpenSearch Service for full-text search and indexing (via DynamoDB Streams) provides the optimal architecture for e-commerce search.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: An industrial manufacturing company is deploying 200,000 IoT temperature sensors in production facilities worldwide. The sensors publish telemetry messages every 5 seconds over MQTT with TLS mutual authentication. The system must ingest the sensor telemetry, route data to a dedicated time-series database optimized for time-series analytics and SQL queries, and trigger automated emergency alarms if temperature exceeds 95°C. Which AWS architecture fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Have all 200,000 sensors send HTTP POST requests directly to an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL database.
options.explanation: Incorrect: 200,000 sensors sending synchronous HTTP POST requests will overwhelm database connections and sensor devices often require lightweight MQTT.

options.text: Store sensor data in Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive and run daily Glue ETL jobs.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Deep Archive has hours of retrieval delay and cannot provide immediate emergency alerting for 95°C temperature breaches.

options.text: Deploy a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances running Mosquitto MQTT brokers in an Auto Scaling group with self-signed SSL certificates.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed MQTT broker clusters require extensive maintenance, patching, and custom certificate lifecycle management compared to serverless AWS IoT Core.

options.text: Connect sensors to AWS IoT Core using X.509 client certificates, use AWS IoT Rules Engine to evaluate temperature thresholds and publish to Amazon SNS for alarms, and route time-series data directly to Amazon Timestream.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS IoT Core supports MQTT with X.509 mTLS authentication. The IoT Rules Engine filters events and routes time-series telemetry natively into Amazon Timestream, with SNS for real-time alerting.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS IoT Core provides secure MQTT communication at scale, while the IoT Rules Engine and Amazon Timestream enable serverless time-series ingestion and real-time alarming.

options.text: Store user passwords in an Amazon RDS MySQL database and write custom PHP authentication scripts on an EC2 instance.

options.text: Create an IAM user for every mobile app customer.
options.explanation: Incorrect: IAM users are for cloud workforce identities and cannot scale to consumer mobile apps.

options.text: Configure an AWS WAF rate-based rule on the API Gateway.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS WAF rate-based rules filter request frequency, but do not provide user authentication, token issuance, or social login.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Cognito User Pools combined with API Gateway Cognito Authorizers provides a fully managed, serverless authentication and authorization solution for web and mobile applications.

options.text: Configure and deploy Enable S3 Versioning on the EBS volumes. following AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: EBS volumes are block devices and do not support S3 Versioning.

options.text: Write a Python script on an EC2 instance that calls `ec2:CreateSnapshot` and `ec2:CopySnapshot` via a cron job.

options.explanation: Incorrect: Attaching 5,000 volumes to one instance exceeds EC2 attachment limits and `dd` is an anti-pattern.

options.text: Configure an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) lifecycle policy targeting EBS volumes tagged `Environment=Production`, defining daily, weekly, and monthly schedules with retention periods and automated cross-region copy rules.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) automates the creation, retention, and cross-region replication of EBS snapshots based on declarative resource tags with zero custom scripting.

options.text: Apply an S3 Bucket Policy with an explicit Deny for `s3:DeleteObject` covering all IAM users.

options.explanation: Incorrect: Governance Mode allows users with specific IAM permissions (s3:BypassGovernanceRetention) or root to alter or delete protected objects.

options.text: Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket and configure Amazon S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode with a default retention period of 5 years.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode enforces a strict WORM (Write Once, Read Many) model where no user, including the root user in the AWS account, can delete objects or reduce retention during the compliance period.

options.explanation: Correct: AWS DMS LOB optimization involves tuning LOB modes: Full LOB mode preserves complete data without truncation, while configuring Inline LOB mode with appropriate buffer sizing and splitting large tables across parallel tasks optimizes throughput.

options.text: Drop all LOB columns from the source SQL Server database before migration.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Dropping production LOB data causes permanent data loss and violates application integrity.

options.text: Switch AWS DMS replication engine to single-threaded sequential mode on a t3.nano instance.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Single-threaded mode on a tiny instance severely degrades replication performance.

options.text: Use AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway to mirror the database.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storage Gateway does not convert schemas between heterogeneous database engines (SQL Server to PostgreSQL).

questions.generalExplanation: Optimizing AWS DMS for Large Binary Objects (LOBs) requires configuring Full LOB or Inline LOB modes with custom LOB chunk sizes and parallel task distribution.

questions.statement: An enterprise CFO requires a comprehensive Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) business case comparison before committing to migrating 2,000 on-premises servers to AWS. The analysis must model multiple migration scenarios (including Bring-Your-Own-License vs AWS-provided licensing, compute right-sizing based on actual historical CPU/RAM utilization, and optimal AWS purchasing options like Compute Savings Plans). Which AWS service provides this business case analysis?

options.text: Use AWS Migration Evaluator (formerly TSO Logic) to analyze on-premises inventory and model total cost of ownership business cases.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Migration Evaluator provides complimentary business case modeling and total cost of ownership (TCO) analysis, analyzing actual on-premises compute utilization and software licensing (Microsoft SQL/Windows) to project optimized AWS spend.

options.text: Download compliance reports and regulatory certifications from the AWS Artifact self-service portal.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Artifact provides compliance audit reports.

options.text: Use AWS Pricing Calculator to model architecture costs before provisioning AWS infrastructure resources.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Pricing Calculator requires manual input of each resource and does not automatically analyze actual on-premises server inventory or software licensing optimization.

options.text: Configure AWS Budgets to send automated notifications when monthly spending limits exceed predefined thresholds.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Budgets is for setting spending limits on existing AWS accounts.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Migration Evaluator (formerly TSO Logic) builds data-driven business cases for cloud migration by analyzing on-premises inventory and optimizing for compute right-sizing and software licensing.
